key_insight: Open-weights, naturally censored LLMs are a realistic and diverse testbed for studying secret-knowledge elicitation and lie detection, exhibiting different failure modes than synthetic liar models and revealing gaps in current honesty-elicitation and detection methods.
problem_solved: Existing evaluations rely on models artificially trained to lie or conceal information, which may not reflect real-world censorship or concealment; this paper provides a natural benchmark and analysis framework to study how to elicit or detect hidden information from realistically censored models.
method: Collect and analyze open-weights LLMs that have been censored or constrained (from Chinese model developers) to create a natural secret-knowledge dataset.
Apply and compare honesty-elicitation strategies (prompting and lightweight interventions) and lie-detection classifiers to elicit or flag concealed outputs.
Contrast performance and failure modes against synthetic liar/concealing models to identify evaluation gaps and practical robustness issues.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners a more realistic evaluation bed for safety and red-team testing, improving understanding of when prompting or detectors succeed or fail in the wild and guiding better defenses and benchmarking practices.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: censored LLMs → elicitation prompts / detectors → labeled outcomes (revealed / concealed / false)
Comparison bar chart: elicitation success and detection accuracy across censored vs synthetic liar models
Heatmap or matrix of failure modes: prompt types × model behaviors (e.g., evasive, hallucinate, refuse)
Icons: locked padlock (censorship), magnifying glass (elicitation), warning sign (safety risks), checklist (benchmark)
paper_title: Censored LLMs as a Natural Testbed for Secret Knowledge Elicitation
paper_authors: Helena Casademunt, Bartosz Cywiński, Khoi Tran, Arya Jakkli, Samuel Marks
